PRINT AT 100% / ACTUAL SIZE
DISABLE FIT TO PAGE / shrink to fit / scale to fit. Measure the ruler before use: 0 to 100 must read 100.0 mm and the cross-check bar 50.0 mm (±0.5). If either is off, do not use the sheet: reprint.

Print every sheet at 100 % / Actual size on portrait A4; every page is portrait, the T4 strips are printed sideways and read that way. Then lay a steel rule on the ruler below. Use the sheets only if 0 to 100 reads 100.0 mm and the bar reads 50.0 mm. A sheet that is 1 % small puts a hole 0.5 mm off at 50 mm.

The print dialog is the usual culprit. Chromium's default for a PDF is Fit to printable area and Firefox's is Fit to page width; both shrink to the printer's imageable area (97.3 % on the Brother HL-2140, measured 1 Nov 2026: the ruler read 97.3). A typed scale is ignored until the mode is Custom or Actual size. The sure way is to send the file to CUPS with scaling off: lp -d HL-2140-series -o media=A4 -o print-scaling=none -P 1 Drilling-and-Placement-Templates.pdf, measure the ruler, then -P 2-25 for the rest. Never add -o landscape: CUPS re-fits whatever it rotates. Check the queue's default paper too (lpoptions -l): it was Letter.

Using a drilling sheet: trim on the heavy datum line(s), butt the trimmed edge to the named edge, tape, then punch each DRILL centre through the paper with an awl or automatic centre punch, lift the sheet and drill to the depth stated. The printed jigs (P18) are the primary tools; these sheets reproduce their patterns and serve as the check. Top marking is done face down (underside up); every pattern here is used without flipping the sheet.
